combat_history.event: PLA fired DF-21D and DF-26 missiles into the South China Sea during exercises; U.S. officials reported a missile struck near or on a moving target ship.
combat_history.significance: First public indication the ASBM concept had been demonstrated against a manoeuvring maritime target.

combat_history.event: DF-21D publicly paraded in Beijing, officially confirming the anti-ship variant.
combat_history.significance: Open acknowledgement of a capability long assessed by Western analysts.

modernization.description: Tighter fusion of OTH radar, Yaogan satellites and UAVs to shorten the targeting cycle.
modernization.impact: Kill-chain timeliness, not the missile itself, is the decisive variable.

vulnerabilities.description: Effectiveness hinges on detecting, tracking and continuously cueing a distant moving ship.
vulnerabilities.context: Severing ISR or datalinks neutralises the weapon without intercepting it.
vulnerabilities.mitigation: Redundant satellite, radar, sub and air sensors.

vulnerabilities.description: The MaRV must reacquire the target against decoys, chaff, jamming and manoeuvre.
vulnerabilities.context: Carrier groups can spoof or evade in the missile's final seconds.

vulnerabilities.description: Never tested against a carrier with full Aegis/SM-3/SM-6 defences and EW.
vulnerabilities.mitigation: Saturation salvos with DF-26 and cruise missiles.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Road-mobile TEL units dispersed and concealed inland; salvo launch on satellite/OTH cueing during a maritime crisis.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Networked with Yaogan ISR satellites, OTH-B radar, submarines and maritime patrol aircraft.
operational_patterns.readiness_notes: Fielded since ~2010; complemented by DF-26 and DF-17.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: DF-26 roughly doubles range to ~4,000 km ('Guam killer') with both land-attack and anti-ship roles.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: Carrier killer vs Guam killer — the reach of China's ASBMs.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: Zircon is a sea/air-launched hypersonic cruise missile, not a land-based ballistic weapon.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: Ballistic vs hypersonic-cruise paths to killing ships.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: LRASM is a stealthy subsonic air/ship-launched cruise missile with autonomous targeting — a very different anti-ship philosophy.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: Mass-and-speed vs stealth-and-autonomy in anti-ship warfare.

doctrine.role: Land-based anti-ship ballistic missile to threaten and deter hostile carrier strike groups approaching China's near seas.
doctrine.employment: Dispersed mobile launchers fire on satellite/OTH cueing; the MaRV manoeuvres to strike a moving ship in its terminal phase.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Impose cost and risk on naval power projection cheaply, exploiting the asymmetry between a missile and a multi-billion-dollar carrier.
doctrine.threat_context: The signature weapon of China's A2/AD strategy and the reason U.S. carrier operations inside the first island chain are now contested.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read alongside the DF-26 and DF-17 as a layered, land-based reconnaissance-strike complex aimed at the sea.
